EFW_Atlas.name: Atlas
EFW_Atlas.role: A name attached to a returning record of planetary ruin
EFW_Atlas.notes: Episode 3 does not explain what Atlas was. The name accompanies a remembered image of civilization-scale collapse. Treat Atlas as historical presence, not software or an AI transmission.

EFW_Tyrus.name: Tyrus
EFW_Tyrus.notes: Worldly, transactional and impatient with mystical claims until he personally sees the past intrude on the present. He speaks like someone who moves contraband for a living, not a physicist.

EFW_Jace.name: Jace
EFW_Jace.role: Vael-Tor platform worker who helps Rae save a refugee transport
EFW_Jace.notes: Practical and protective. Jace repeatedly tries to bring Rae back to her own physical limits while she focuses on the people trapped above them.

EFW_Ryn.name: Ryn
EFW_Ryn.role: Dockmaster controlling access to outbound skiffs
EFW_Ryn.notes: Transactional and suspicious. Ryn wants the shard off the platform once its presence makes forgotten architecture visible.

EFW_Vyn.name: Vyn
EFW_Vyn.role: Orbital controller responsible for Vael-Tor dock safety
EFW_Vyn.notes: A present-day authority facing an ugly choice. Vyn is willing to destroy a damaged refugee transport to protect the platforms. His conflict with Rae is moral and procedural, not mathematical.

EFW_Vorken.name: Vorken
EFW_Vorken.role: Black-market enforcer pursuing Theo on the Vael-Tor promenade
EFW_Vorken.notes: Physically confident and accustomed to frightened couriers. His confrontation exposes remembered combat reflexes in Theo and leaves bystanders witnessing an impossible shadow of the ancient war.
